meta.name: InterviewQ Bank
meta.description: Curated + pattern-based knowledge base of interview questions, role/topic taxonomies, company-specific patterns, and learning resources. Serves as the retrieval corpus for the RAG pipeline.

amazon.label: Amazon
themes: Amazon Leadership Principles: Customer Obsession, Ownership, Deliver Results, Dive Deep
Bar raiser rounds are heavily STAR-formatted

microsoft.label: Microsoft
themes: Expect 'tell me about a time' questions mapped to competencies

meta.label: Meta
themes: Move fast, ship mindset, product sense

flipkart.label: Flipkart / E-commerce
themes: E-commerce scale: flash sales, traffic spikes, seller ecosystem
Expect STAR stories about owning outcomes end to end

services.label: IT Services (Infosys/TCS/Wipro)
themes: Process discipline, client communication, onboarding speed
Expect HR + situational judgment + basic technical

dsa: LeetCode Top 150 — solve 2 problems daily, time-boxed
NeetCode Roadmap — structured DSA revision path
system-design: System Design Primer (GitHub) — fundamentals to advanced
ByteByteGo — architecture deep dives and diagrams
databases: Use The Index, Luke! — SQL indexing explained
backend: System Design Interview (Alex Xu) — backend patterns
frontend: MDN Web Docs — the core frontend reference
React docs — 'Thinking in React' & state management
web: MDN HTTP — status codes, caching, headers
os: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces (free book)
CS 162 UC Berkeley lecture notes on concurrency
ml: Hugging Face Course — transformers, NLP, fine-tuning
product: Cracking the PM Interview — frameworks & cases
metrics: Evan Miller — A/B testing statistics made simple
Amplitude / GA4 analytics courses — metric design
devops: roadmap.sh DevOps — CI/CD, Docker, IaC path
behavioral: STAR method workbook — 5 core stories (failure, conflict, initiative, leadership, results)
Amazon LPs / competency frameworks — map each story to a principle
hr: Practice a 1-minute intro + 'Why this company' out loud
Common HR questions bank — strengths, weaknesses, 5-year plan
communication: Practice answers aloud with a timer — aim for 90 seconds per STAR story

questions.text: Tell me about yourself.
idealPoints: 1-minute structured intro: current role → relevant experience → why this role/company
Mention 2-3 achievements with numbers, not just duties
End with a forward-looking sentence tying to the role
followUps: Walk me through the most relevant project on your resume in a bit more detail.
What made you pivot/choose this career path?

questions.text: Why do you want to work here, and why should we hire you?
idealPoints: Connect company mission/products to your own values and skills
Show specific research about the team or product
Differentiate yourself with one concrete strength + proof
followUps: What do you know about our recent product launches or roadmap?
What would you want to accomplish in your first 90 days?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you failed or made a significant mistake. What did you do?
idealPoints: Own the failure without blaming others
Describe what you did to fix it and prevent recurrence
Share a concrete lesson that changed your behavior
followUps: What would you do differently if you faced the same situation today?
How did your team or manager react?

questions.text: Describe a time you disagreed with a teammate or manager about a technical or product decision.
idealPoints: Frame the disagreement around data/evidence, not ego
Explain how you voiced it constructively
End with the outcome and what you learned about persuasion
followUps: Did you ever agree just to move forward even though you disagreed? When?
How do you handle it when you lose the argument?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you received difficult feedback. How did you respond?
idealPoints: Show receptiveness rather than defensiveness
Describe the concrete change you made after the feedback
Mention the result if possible
followUps: How do you typically ask for feedback proactively?
Who gives you the most useful feedback and why?

questions.text: Describe a time you worked under a tight deadline or high pressure. How did you manage it?
idealPoints: Describe prioritization and triage approach
Explain communication with stakeholders
Include the outcome and what you'd repeat
followUps: What did you deprioritize or drop, and how did you decide?
How do you keep calm under pressure personally?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you took initiative beyond your assigned responsibilities.
idealPoints: Describe the gap you noticed and the idea you proposed
Show how you got buy-in or executed without being asked
Quantify the impact
followUps: Was there pushback? How did you handle it?
Did you ever have to do extra work to make it happen?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you led a team or mentored someone. What was your approach?
idealPoints: Describe the situation and your leadership style
Show how you set direction and supported the person
Mention the outcome for the team/mentee
followUps: How do you handle an underperforming team member?
How do you delegate without micromanaging?

questions.text: How do you stay updated with the latest technologies and industry trends?
idealPoints: Name specific sources (docs, newsletters, courses, communities)
Show a habit with consistency, e.g., weekly learning block
Tie it back to applying knowledge at work
followUps: What is the most recent thing you learned that you've used?
How much time do you realistically spend on learning per week?

questions.text: What are your strengths and weaknesses?
idealPoints: Pick strengths relevant to the role with evidence
Pick a real weakness (not a disguised strength) plus mitigation
Keep it concise and honest
followUps: How has that weakness affected you at work recently?
What are you doing to work on it right now?

questions.text: Where do you see yourself in five years?
idealPoints: Align growth ambitions with the company's trajectory
Show commitment to the role, not a generic answer
Mention skills you want to build
followUps: How does this role fit into that plan?
What would you need to learn to get there?

questions.text: Do you have any questions for us?
idealPoints: Ask about the team, product roadmap, or success metrics
Ask about growth and what excellence looks like here
Avoid salary/timing-only questions
followUps: What does a typical week look like in this role?
What's the biggest challenge the team is facing right now?

questions.text: Explain how a hash map works under the hood. When would you choose it over other data structures?
idealPoints: Explain hash function → bucket/index, collisions, chaining vs open addressing
Mention average O(1) get/put, worst-case O(n)
Give tradeoffs vs arrays/lists/sets and a real use case
followUps: How would you handle poor hash distribution?
What is a load factor and why does resizing matter?

questions.text: How would you find the kth largest element in an array efficiently?
idealPoints: Mention sorting (O(n log n)), min-heap of size k (O(n log k))
Mention Quickselect with average O(n)
Discuss tradeoffs and when each fits
followUps: How would you modify the approach for a stream of data?
What's the worst case for Quickselect and how do you mitigate it?

questions.text: Design an LRU cache from scratch. Walk me through the data structures and operations.
idealPoints: HashMap for O(1) lookup + doubly linked list for O(1) eviction
Explain get (move to head) and put (evict tail when full)
Discuss thread-safety options and alternatives (LFU)
followUps: How would you make this thread-safe in a multithreaded server?
What if access patterns make LRU perform poorly?

questions.text: Explain Big-O notation. Give examples of common complexities and why they matter in production.
idealPoints: Define Big-O as asymptotic growth of operations vs input
Give examples: O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n²) with concrete code
Tie to real tradeoffs (sorting, nested loops, binary search)
followUps: What's the complexity of binary search and what precondition does it need?
Can you give an example where a worse Big-O is still the right choice?

questions.text: How would you implement a binary search? What are the edge cases?
idealPoints: Explain the divide-and-conquer invariant and O(log n) time
Mention sorted precondition and integer overflow in mid
Handle not-found termination correctly
followUps: Write the boundary conditions you'd check in a code review.
How do you find the first occurrence of a duplicate value?

questions.text: Write a function to reverse a linked list. Walk me through the logic.
idealPoints: Iterative approach with prev/current/next pointers
Mention the recursive alternative
Handle empty list and single-node edge cases
followUps: What's the time and space complexity of each approach?
How would you reverse a linked list in groups of k?

questions.text: How would you detect a cycle in a linked list? Compare the approaches.
idealPoints: Hash-set of visited nodes (O(n) space)
Floyd's tortoise-and-hare (O(1) space)
Explain why hare/fast steps of 2 works
followUps: How would you find the start node of the cycle?
What if the list is huge and fits in memory only partially?

questions.text: Find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters. Describe your algorithm.
idealPoints: Sliding window with a set/map of characters
Explain O(n) time, O(min(m, alphabet)) space
Walk through the window shrink on duplicates
followUps: How would you return the substring itself, not just the length?
What if the string can contain unicode or emojis?

questions.text: Explain Dijkstra's algorithm and when it fails.
idealPoints: Explain priority-queue BFS with greedy relaxation, O((V+E) log V)
State requirement: non-negative edge weights
Mention use in routing/maps and alternative (Bellman-Ford) for negative weights
followUps: Why does Dijkstra fail with negative weights?
How would you handle a dense graph — is there a better approach?

questions.text: Design a URL shortener like bit.ly. Walk me through the core components.
idealPoints: API design: POST to shorten, GET redirect for short code
Short code generation: base62, hashing, or counter + collision handling
Storage, caching (Redis TTL), 301 vs 302, analytics
Scale: read-heavy, horizontal scaling, consistent hashing
followUps: How do you generate unique short codes at scale?
How would you support custom aliases and expiry?

questions.text: Design a rate limiter. What algorithms exist and which would you choose?
idealPoints: Define the requirement (per-user/per-IP, sliding vs fixed window)
Compare fixed window, sliding log, sliding window counter, token bucket, leaky bucket
Discuss Redis-based distributed implementation and headers (X-RateLimit-*)
Mention graceful degradation (429, retry-after)
followUps: How do you rate limit across multiple data centers?
What happens when the rate limiter itself fails?

questions.text: Design a chat application (1:1 and group). What are the key architectural pieces?
idealPoints: Realtime transport: WebSockets vs long-polling
Message flow: send → server → fan-out to recipients
Storage: message DB, sequence numbers, read receipts
Presence, offline handling, and horizontal scaling of connections
followUps: How do you guarantee message ordering across devices?
How would you implement read receipts efficiently?

questions.text: Design a recommendation system for a shopping app. Walk me through data and algorithms.
idealPoints: Offline: collaborative filtering (user-item) and content-based features
Cold start handling: popular items, embeddings, session-based recs
Online: candidate retrieval + ranking (CTR models)
Metrics: precision@k, CTR, revenue impact, A/B testing
followUps: How do you handle the cold start for new users?
How would you evaluate a new ranking model before rollout?

questions.text: Explain REST vs GraphQL. When would you choose one over the other?
idealPoints: REST: resource-oriented, multiple round trips, over/under-fetching
GraphQL: single endpoint, client-defined shape, typed schema
Tradeoffs: caching, complexity, tooling, N+1 problem
followUps: How do you handle caching with GraphQL?
What are common pitfalls when migrating REST to GraphQL?

questions.text: How does authentication and authorization work? Compare JWT vs session-based.
idealPoints: Authn vs authz distinction
JWT: stateless, signed, verification flow; risks (leakage, no revocation)
Sessions: server-side state, easy revocation, scaling concerns
Mention refresh tokens, HttpOnly cookies, CSRF
followUps: How do you revoke a stolen JWT?
Where should you store tokens in a browser and why?

questions.text: How would you design a background job queue? What guarantees does it need?
idealPoints: Components: producer, queue (Redis/SQS), workers, retries with backoff
At-least-once vs at-most-once vs exactly-once semantics
Dead-letter queue, visibility timeout, idempotent consumers
Observability: job metrics, tracing
followUps: How do you ensure a job is processed exactly once in a distributed system?
What happens if a worker crashes mid-job?

questions.text: What is idempotency and why does it matter in API design?
idealPoints: Define idempotency: same request → same effect
Examples: payment retries, webhooks, POST vs PUT/PATCH semantics
Implementation: idempotency keys, unique constraints, conditional writes
followUps: How would you implement idempotency for a payment endpoint?
How do GETs and webhook replays fit into idempotency?

questions.text: Explain common caching strategies and cache invalidation.
idealPoints: Cache-aside (lazy), write-through, write-behind
TTL, eviction policies, and stampede protection
Invalidation: explicit delete vs TTL vs versioning
Where to cache: CDN, app, DB query cache, Redis
followUps: What is a cache stampede and how do you prevent it?
How do you keep cache and database consistent?

questions.text: Explain database indexing. What are the tradeoffs?
idealPoints: B-tree index: sorted structure enabling fast lookups/ranges
Tradeoffs: write overhead, storage, cardinality
Composite indexes and leftmost prefix rule
When indexes hurt: low selectivity columns, heavy writes
followUps: Why does adding an index slow down writes?
How would you diagnose a slow query — what would you check first?

questions.text: Describe the ACID properties of a transaction.
idealPoints: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability — define each
Give a money-transfer example to illustrate
Mention tradeoffs: ACID vs BASE in distributed systems
followUps: What isolation levels exist and which would you pick?
How do distributed systems relax ACID and why?

questions.text: SQL vs NoSQL: how do you choose which database to use?
idealPoints: SQL: schema, joins, transactions, consistency — good for relational data
NoSQL: flexibility, horizontal scaling, specialized models (doc, key-value, graph, column)
Decision drivers: access patterns, scale, team skills, consistency needs
Mention polyglot persistence as a realistic answer
followUps: When would you use a document DB over a relational one for e-commerce?
What is eventual consistency and when is it acceptable?

questions.text: What is the difference between a process and a thread?
idealPoints: Process: independent memory space, heavier, isolated
Thread: shares process memory, lighter, faster context switch
Concurrency vs parallelism, and when threads are risky
followUps: What is a race condition and how do you prevent it?
How does a context switch work and why is it costly?

questions.text: What is a deadlock? What conditions cause it and how do you prevent it?
idealPoints: Define deadlock: circular wait on resources
List the 4 conditions: mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, circular wait
Prevention: lock ordering, timeouts, single lock, deadlock detection
followUps: Give a real example from database or multithreaded code.
How do databases detect and resolve deadlocks?

questions.text: Explain the virtual DOM and how React uses it.
idealPoints: Virtual DOM = lightweight in-memory representation of UI
Reconciliation: diff old vs new vDOM → minimal DOM updates
Tradeoffs: performance vs complexity; mention compiler-driven alternatives
followUps: What is key prop and why does it matter in lists?
How does React batch state updates?

questions.text: Explain closures in JavaScript with a real example.
idealPoints: Closure = function + lexical environment it was created in
Give example: counter factory, debounce, module pattern
Mention memory implications and common interview traps
followUps: What's the difference between let and var in a loop with closures?
When do closures cause memory leaks?

questions.text: How do you optimize page load time? Walk me through the main levers.
idealPoints: Network: minify, compress (gzip/brotli), CDN, HTTP/2, preload
Rendering: critical CSS, lazy loading, image optimization, code splitting
Measure first: Lighthouse, Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, INP)
Runtime: bundle analysis, tree shaking
followUps: What are Core Web Vitals and how do you improve LCP specifically?
How do you decide what to lazy load?

questions.text: Design an autocomplete search component. What are the key considerations?
idealPoints: Input handling: debounce, abort stale requests, race conditions
Backend: prefix search, ranking, suggestion sources
UX: keyboard navigation, highlight, loading/empty/error states
Performance: local caching, virtualization for long lists
followUps: How do you handle out-of-order responses?
How would you cache suggestions on the client?

questions.text: How would you make a web application accessible?
idealPoints: Semantic HTML, ARIA roles only where needed
Keyboard navigation, focus management, skip links
Contrast, reduced motion, screen reader testing
Automated tools (axe, Lighthouse) + manual testing
followUps: What is WCAG and what levels have you worked with?
How do you test accessibility in CI?

questions.text: Flexbox vs Grid: when do you use each?
idealPoints: Flexbox: one-dimensional layout (row or column)
Grid: two-dimensional layout (rows and columns together)
Practical decision rules and common patterns
followUps: How do you center an element both ways with each?
What's a good use case for grid auto-fit with minmax?

questions.text: How would you implement infinite scroll? What are the pitfalls?
idealPoints: IntersectionObserver on a sentinel element to trigger fetch
Maintain scroll position, dedupe keys, avoid layout thrash
Pitfalls: premature triggers, mobile scroll performance, accessibility (provide alternatives)
Pagination vs infinite scroll tradeoffs
followUps: How do you handle the back button with infinite scroll?
What if the scroll container isn't the window?

questions.text: Explain the event loop in Node.js and how async code is handled.
idealPoints: Single thread + event loop; libuv thread pool for I/O
Microtasks (Promise) vs macrotasks (setTimeout, I/O callbacks)
Why blocking the event loop is dangerous; examples
Worker threads for CPU-heavy work
followUps: What order do promises, setTimeout, and I/O callbacks run in?
How would you profile event loop blockage in production?

questions.text: Explain connection pooling. Why does it matter for database performance?
idealPoints: Creating DB connections is expensive (TCP + handshake + auth)
Pool reuses connections; size tuning (latency × throughput)
Starving pools, timeouts, and how ORMs expose it
followUps: What happens when all pool connections are in use?
How would you size a connection pool for a service?

questions.text: Microservices vs monolith: how do you decide?
idealPoints: Monolith: simpler ops, single deploy, fine for small teams
Microservices: independent scaling, team ownership, fault isolation
Costs: distributed complexity, network, data consistency, observability
Mention modular monolith and start-simple evolution
followUps: What are the hardest operational problems in microservices?
How do you handle distributed transactions across services?

questions.text: Walk me through your approach to testing code.
idealPoints: Testing pyramid: unit → integration → e2e, right balance
Test the behavior not implementation; naming conventions
Coverage as a signal, not a goal; test what matters
CI gating, flaky test handling
followUps: How do you decide what deserves an e2e test?
How do you deal with flaky tests?

questions.text: Walk me through what happens when you type a URL and press Enter.
idealPoints: DNS resolution → TCP/TLS handshake → HTTP request
Server processing → response with headers
Browser parsing (HTML/CSS/JS) → render, layout, paint
Mention caching, CDN, and the layers of the stack
followUps: Where does caching kick in at each step?
What headers affect caching and security (HSTS, CSP)?

questions.text: What is the difference between HTTP and HTTPS, and how does TLS work at a high level?
idealPoints: HTTPS = HTTP over TLS; encryption + authentication
TLS handshake: cert verification, key exchange, session keys
Why mixed content and cert expiry matter
followUps: How does a browser verify a certificate?
What is HSTS and what does it prevent?

questions.text: Walk me through an end-to-end ML project you worked on.
idealPoints: Problem framing + success metrics with stakeholders
Data: collection, cleaning, EDA, feature engineering
Modeling: baseline → candidate models → evaluation
Deployment, monitoring, and iteration loop
followUps: How did you evaluate model performance against business metrics?
What would you do differently next time?

questions.text: Explain precision vs recall, and how you choose between them.
idealPoints: Precision: of predicted positives, how many were right
Recall: of actual positives, how many were found
Tradeoff and the F1 harmonic mean; PR vs ROC curves
Domain examples: fraud (precision) vs disease screening (recall)
followUps: What is the area under the ROC curve and its limitation with imbalanced data?
In fraud detection, which do you prioritize and why?

questions.text: How do you handle imbalanced datasets?
idealPoints: Understand the problem: rare positives, cost of errors
Data: resampling (SMOTE), class weights, synthetic data
Modeling: use PR-AUC instead of accuracy, calibration
Framing: anomaly detection or two-stage pipelines for extreme imbalance
followUps: Why is accuracy a bad metric for imbalanced data?
What is SMOTE and what are its pitfalls?

questions.text: Explain the bias-variance tradeoff.
idealPoints: Bias: error from overly simple assumptions; variance: sensitivity to training data
Underfitting vs overfitting relationship
How to diagnose: train/val error gap, learning curves
Mitigations: regularization, more data, ensemble methods
followUps: How would you detect overfitting without a test set?
How do regularization parameters (e.g., lambda) affect bias and variance?

questions.text: How does gradient descent work? What are the variants and pitfalls?
idealPoints: Iteratively move parameters opposite the gradient to minimize loss
Learning rate: too high diverges, too low slow; scheduling
Variants: batch, SGD, mini-batch, momentum, Adam
Pitfalls: local minima, saddle points, feature scaling
followUps: Why is feature scaling important for gradient descent?
How does learning rate scheduling help training?

questions.text: How would you build a fraud detection system for transactions?
idealPoints: Label/ground truth issues: definition of fraud, delay in labels
Features: transaction velocity, amount anomalies, device/location signals
Model: gradient boosting + threshold tuning on PR curve
Deployment: real-time scoring, drift monitoring, human review loop
followUps: How do you handle concept drift in fraud patterns?
How would you measure the business impact of the model?

questions.text: What is overfitting and how do you prevent it?
idealPoints: Model fits training noise, generalizes poorly
Prevention: more data, regularization, simpler models, early stopping, cross-validation
Diagnosis via train/test error gap
followUps: How does dropout help in neural networks?
What is the difference between validation and test sets?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you designed or analyzed an A/B test.
idealPoints: Hypothesis + primary/secondary metrics, guardrail metrics
Sample size, randomization, duration and novelty effects
Statistical significance, practical significance, segmentation
Result → decision and lessons learned
followUps: What is peeking and why is it a problem?
What would you do if the test result conflicts with your intuition?

questions.text: How do you prioritize features when everything is urgent?
idealPoints: Frame with user value, business impact, effort/risk
Frameworks: RICE, MoSCoW, impact/effort matrix
Bring data + stakeholder alignment to the decision
Show willingness to say no and revisit
followUps: How do you handle a stakeholder who disagrees with the priority?
Which framework do you actually use day-to-day and why?

questions.text: What is the difference between an MVP and a prototype? How do you decide what to build first?
idealPoints: Prototype: validate desirability/feasibility, throwaway
MVP: smallest thing that delivers value and enables learning
Decision driven by the biggest risk to validate
Example walkthrough
followUps: What's the riskiest assumption in your current product and how would you test it?
How do you keep an MVP from becoming a prototype?

questions.text: Design a feature for an existing product you use often.
idealPoints: Choose product, define target user and problem with evidence
Explore solutions, pick one with tradeoffs, define scope
Define success metrics and rollout plan
Show user empathy and prioritization discipline
followUps: What would you build in the first version vs later?
How would you measure whether it worked?

questions.text: How do you measure product success?
idealPoints: North star metric tied to value delivered
Input vs output metrics; leading vs lagging
Examples: activation, retention, engagement, revenue
Balance: don't optimize a single metric at the expense of health
followUps: What's your north star for an e-commerce app and why?
Which counter-metrics would you watch?

questions.text: Tell me about a product you improved. How did you decide what to change?
idealPoints: Describe the product and the problem with user evidence
Explain the process: research → prioritization → build → measure
Quantify the impact
Reflect on what you'd do differently
followUps: Who did you involve in the decision?
What did you learn from the users during research?

questions.text: Walk me through a launch you led. What did you own?
idealPoints: Scope: who, what, when; cross-functional coordination
Risks and rollback plan; go/no-go criteria
Launch execution + post-launch metrics and iteration
Show leadership and communication
followUps: What went wrong during that launch?
How did you coordinate engineering, design, and marketing?

questions.text: What metrics would you track for a subscription product? Build a metric tree.
idealPoints: Acquisition → activation → engagement → retention → revenue → referral
Key ratios: conversion, churn, LTV, CAC, MRR/ARR, expansion revenue
Explain leading indicators and guardrails
Tie each metric to a decision it informs
followUps: What is the most important metric and why?
How would you reduce churn?

questions.text: How do you handle a stakeholder who blocks your initiative?
idealPoints: Understand their concerns and incentives first
Find data and allies; propose a smaller test
Escalate transparently if needed; build trust over time
Example from experience
followUps: When would you push back on a stakeholder?
How do you rebuild a relationship after disagreement?

questions.text: Explain CI/CD. What are the core components of a pipeline?
idealPoints: CI: build + test on every merge; fast feedback
CD: automated deploy through environments with gates
Stages: lint → unit → build artifact → staging → canary → prod
Quality gates, artifact promotion, rollback
followUps: How do you handle secrets in CI/CD?
What's the difference between continuous delivery and continuous deployment?

questions.text: How does Kubernetes schedule pods? Explain the scheduler's decision process.
idealPoints: Scheduling = binding pods to nodes via kube-scheduler
Filtering (feasibility: resources, taints) then scoring (spread, affinity)
QoS classes and eviction under pressure
Hand-rolled scheduling vs cluster autoscaling
followUps: What is the difference between limits and requests?
What happens when a node goes down?

questions.text: Explain blue-green vs canary deployments.
idealPoints: Blue-green: two identical environments, instant switch, easy rollback
Canary: gradual % traffic shift with monitoring gates
Tradeoffs: cost, complexity, state/db compatibility
When each fits
followUps: What database migration issues do you hit with blue-green?
What metrics would gate a canary promotion?

questions.text: You get paged for a service outage at 3 AM. Walk me through your process.
idealPoints: Stabilize first: mitigate (rollback, scale, failover) before deep diagnosis
Communicate status to stakeholders; maintain a timeline
Post-incident: blameless postmortem, action items, prevention
Show calm prioritization
followUps: How do you decide to roll back vs roll forward?
What makes a good postmortem?

questions.text: How do you debug a slow API in production?
idealPoints: Reproduce and instrument: APM traces, metrics, logs
Check tiers: client → network → LB → app → DB → third-party
Common causes: N+1 queries, missing index, lock contention, GC
Measure before and after the fix
followUps: What if the slowness is intermittent?
How do you add tracing to a legacy system?

questions.text: Design monitoring and alerting for a new microservice.
idealPoints: RED vs USE metrics: rate, errors, duration / utilization, saturation
Logs, metrics, and traces; correlation via request ID
Alert on symptoms with runbooks, not noise; alert fatigue
SLIs → SLOs → error budgets
followUps: What is an error budget and how do you use it?
How do you avoid alert fatigue?

questions.text: How do you decide what to automate vs test manually?
idealPoints: Automate stable, high-value, repeatable flows; ROI analysis
Manual for exploratory, usability, visual, one-off scenarios
Pyramid: many unit, fewer integration, fewest e2e
Flakiness and maintenance cost considerations
followUps: How do you sell automation investment to management?
What's your approach to keeping UI tests stable?

questions.text: Design a test plan for a checkout page. What would you cover?
idealPoints: Functional: happy path, validation, payment gateways, coupons, errors
Edge: currency, tax, failed payments, timeout, double-click prevention
Cross-browser, mobile, accessibility
Priority, risk-based approach, and automation split
followUps: How do you test payment failure handling?
What data would you need to prepare?

questions.text: Explain the testing pyramid.
idealPoints: Base: fast, numerous unit tests
Middle: integration tests for module interactions
Top: few, slow, brittle e2e tests
Why inverted pyramids are a smell
followUps: Where would contract testing fit in?
Why are e2e tests slow and brittle?

questions.text: How do you write a good bug report?
idealPoints: Reproducible steps, environment, expected vs actual
Severity/priority, attachments/logs, affected versions
Clear title; avoid vague 'it doesn't work'
Communication with devs for triage
followUps: What makes a bug unreproducible and what do you do?
How do you prioritize which bugs to fix first?

questions.text: Tell me about the hardest technical problem you've solved.
idealPoints: Set up the context and why it was hard
Walk through your investigation and the aha moment
Explain the solution and its impact with numbers
Show resilience and depth
followUps: What other approaches did you try first?
How long did it take and how did you keep going?

questions.text: Design a news feed for a social app. How do you balance freshness and relevance?
idealPoints: Fan-out on write vs on read; hybrid approaches
Ranking signals: recency, affinity, engagement
Storage and caching: precomputed feeds, pagination with cursors
Scaling: sharding, caching layers, degradation
followUps: How do you handle the celebrity (super-connector) problem?
